## Linked Issue

Fixes #5182

The linked issue carries `confirmed-bug`. This PR follows @trek-e's diagnosis and Agent Brief on the issue (issuecomment-5963253983); its six acceptance criteria are mapped below. Out of scope, per the brief: #2699 (general subagent watchdog) and #3923 (threshold default).

---

## What was broken

With the default `planner.stall_detection_enabled: true`, `/gsd:plan-phase` decides that a background planner or plan-checker has finished by grepping the host's `{outputFile}` for the return markers. On Claude Code that file is the subagent transcript. The transcript already holds the agent's prompt and its definition snapshot, and both quote the markers, so the wait reported `marker_received` at its first check whether or not the agent had returned. The revision watch passed no markers, so every revision round could only end in the "Accept as revised / Retry / Stop" stall menu. A host that returns no output file could only ever reach `stalled`.

## What this fix does

Each watched spawn now gets a GSD-owned, per-dispatch return receipt, and the watch reads only that file:

- `gsd_receipt_path "${PHASE_DIR}" <spawn> "${PROJECT_ROOT}"` prints a fresh absolute path, `<phase>/.gsd-returns/<spawn>.<epoch>.XXXXXXXX`. It creates the directory with a catch-all `.gitignore` but not the file. `PROJECT_ROOT` is init's `project_root`; with no third argument the orchestrator's `pwd -P` is used.
  - It fails closed (prints nothing, returns 1) unless the phase directory's nearest existing ancestor resolves, with `pwd -P`, under that root, and no walked component, `.gsd-returns` or its `.gitignore` is a symlink.
  - It also fails closed on a `.` or `..` component, and on a quote, `$`, a backtick, `<`, `>` or any control character in the phase path.
  - Every refusal prints one `gsd_receipt_path: no receipt: <reason>` line on stderr.
  - Only static, checked-in links are in scope; the check-then-act race is not.
  - The orchestrator binds the printed path as `{receipt}` in the spawn prompt (`<return_receipt>{receipt}</return_receipt>`) and in the watch call.
- The agent's last action is to write the marker line it returns to that path with the Write tool.
- `gsd_return_marker FILE MARKER...` is the single owner of "which marker did the agent return":
  - It does a literal line-start match within the first 64 lines and 4096 bytes.
  - The marker must end within those 4096 bytes, and it must be followed by the end of the line, whitespace, CR or a colon. 4097 bytes are read, so a word cut at the cap never matches.
  - It ignores a receipt that is a symlink. It tolerates a BOM on line 1 and a missing final newline.
  - `gsd_stall_watch` uses it for `marker_found`, and step 11 routes the checker on it, so the watch and the router cannot disagree. Prompt, definition and JSONL transcript text never match it.
- The revision watch passes `## REVISION COMPLETE` and `## REVISION_CONFLICT`, so it has a success exit. `## REVISION COMPLETE` was already emitted (`planner-revision.md` Step 7). It is now declared in gsd-planner's Return Markers and in the `agent-contracts.md` registry.
- A real completion result arriving between cycles ends the wait. The receipt carries only the marker, so every route that needs the body fails closed when the body has not arrived:
  - `## ISSUES FOUND` goes to 11a.
  - A planner checkpoint, split or Source Audit goes to 9a.
  - `## REVISION_CONFLICT` goes to the revision stalled menu, with Retry offered first.
- A `$TS` lost between tool calls falls back to the epoch stamped into the receipt name.

All five watch sites get the receipt, and each rule removes it with `rm -f "{receipt}"` after routing any result, stalled and Retry included. Three are the `plan-phase.md` steps the brief names (8, 10, 12). The other two are the chunked outline and per-plan sites in `steps/chunked-planning-mode.md`.

## Root cause

`gsd_stall_watch` ran `grep -qF` over the whole host output file. On Claude Code that file contains the agent's inputs as well as its output. The revision call site passed no markers, so the `marker_received` exit in `gsd_stall_should_recover` was unreachable for it. Introduced by 067a4d1c6c (#3015). `gsd_stall_should_recover` itself is unchanged on purpose.

## Checker posture (maintainer decision, issuecomment-6036744404; review 5563209291 Major 1)

gsd-plan-checker moves from #767 Group A to Group B. Its `tools:` gains `Write` for the receipt, and its Claude `disallowedTools` becomes `Edit, MultiEdit`. Codex derives `workspace-write` from its `tools:`. The receipt rule and `<anti_patterns>` both say that the receipt is the checker's only write.

**Scoped per host.** OpenCode, Kilo and Copilot grant Write and Edit as one `edit` permission. There the installer drops the checker's `Write` before conversion (`scopeReceiptOnlyWrite`, at the ADR-1235 descriptor boundary), so the checker keeps its read-only posture, edit stays denied, and no checker receipt is written. A `Write` the user grants in `agent_tools` is appended afterwards and kept. A test derives the set of merging hosts from every descriptor agent converter's real output and requires the table to equal it.

Hosts that keep a separate write tool keep the checker's `Write`: Claude Code, Antigravity (`write_file`), Pi (`write`), Hermes, ZCode, Qwen, and Kimi CLI (`WriteFile`). Augment, Cline, CodeBuddy, Cursor, Trae and Windsurf emit no tool restriction at all, so they are unchanged. On kimi-code the planner and checker map to built-ins that cannot write, so no receipt is written there.

**Security posture, stated plainly:** on the hosts that keep `Write`, the "only write" limit is prose, as it is for the other Group B agents.
